A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LOGLO-FNO and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Retained material can be matched across the substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-operator experiments on Kolmogorov Flow, Diffusion-Reaction, and Turbulent Radiative Layer 3D, including quantitative comparisons and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on three further PDE problems, component ablations, super-resolution, computational cost, and variability across runs.

M1.justification: The architecture, adaptive noise, SPHERE loss, and optional attention-fusion variant remain. However, Section 3.2 and Appendix D.2 revise the radial-loss normalization from 1/(Nx Ny Lx Ly) to (Lx/Nx)(Ly/Ny). This changes the general loss definition, although both pseudocode versions set Lx=Ly=1, making their implemented factors equivalent.

E1.justification: v2 adds compressible Navier-Stokes turbulence, Wave-Gauss acoustic propagation, and the compressible Euler four-quadrant Riemann problem, extending evaluation to additional turbulent, wave, and shock phenomena. Appendix L also introduces actual zero-shot spatial super-resolution tests; v1 only discusses that capability.

E2.justification: Transolver is added to the retained Kolmogorov Flow and Diffusion-Reaction comparisons. The TRL3D comparison expands beyond v1's FNO, U-Net, and CNextU-Net to include LSM, differential-kernel NO-LIDK, and reported FNO/TFNO results from The Well. Appendix M additionally compares runtime with Athena++.

E3.justification: The main TRL3D configurations change from 18 to 12 global modes; LOGLO-FNO also changes from 48 to 52 channels and from learning rate 0.0044 to 0.0040. New protocols include time-averaged rollout windows, cross-resolution evaluation, controlled component/patch-size experiments, and hardware timing benchmarks. These extend beyond newly disclosed settings.

E4.justification: v2 replaces the Kolmogorov component-ablation tables in v1 Appendix K with fuller TRL3D loss/HFP isolation studies. It adds patch-size sensitivity, adaptive-noise and radial-cutoff ablations, TRL3D mode sensitivity, super-resolution robustness, and shock-error visualizations. The existing attention/SPHERE study and much spectral and correlation analysis remain.

E5.justification: v1 does not report seed-based experimental uncertainty. v2 Appendix N reports four-seed comparisons with 95% confidence intervals; Appendix K adds repeated-run means and standard deviations, including five-seed cutoff tests. Runtime measurements also gain repetition counts and uncertainty. Appendix K.5 explicitly discloses excluding one unstable run from its three-run summary.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive benchmark, ablation, super-resolution, uncertainty, and runtime results while largely retaining the original Kolmogorov and Diffusion-Reaction scores. New Wave-Gauss results favor LSM on nRMSE but LOGLO-FNO on mid/high-frequency errors. TRL3D scores are replaced under revised configurations, so their numerical differences do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 3 specializes the general input-dependent local kernel to a convolutional kernel depending on x-y. Algorithm 1 corrects the formal radial aggregation and indexing, alongside the revised loss normalization. Appendix F's complexity derivations remain; the expanded descriptions of existing metrics do not constitute new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion broaden the stated scope of demonstrated effectiveness to wave propagation and shock problems. The central architectural contributions, frequency-aware loss, and up-to-50% parameter-saving claim remain. Rollout stability is more prominent in the abstract but was already claimed and investigated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of remaining shock-related errors, degradation during resolution transfer, patch-size and cutoff tradeoffs, and computational overhead. Appendix M distinguishes parameter efficiency from execution efficiency by acknowledging roughly 3.3-fold slower training and inference than base FNO in the reported comparison. These materially clarify practical limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices B, M, and O substantially expand data preparation, baseline configurations, batch sizes, hardware, and timing procedures. v2 specifies the H100 benchmarking environment and explains measured versus extrapolated trajectory runtimes. It also adds project-page access information and clearer 3D patch specifications; the PyTorch/NumPy implementation basis is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Poseidon, Transolver, Athena++, and Schwarz et al. on frequency bias. Appendix A more explicitly distinguishes patchwise spectral convolution and HFP from NO-LIDK. The broader related-work narrative and identification of NO-LIDK as the closest comparator remain.

P1.justification: Much existing prose and the overall narrative remain. v2 clarifies tensor notation, expands metric explanations and the symbol glossary, reorders parameter-budget subsections, moves Algorithm 1 into the appendix, and separates main-text ablations from detailed appendix results. These are targeted editorial and structural refinements rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: Main comparison tables are redesigned as compact metric summaries, with full tables placed in Appendix G.2. v2 enlarges and relabels the architecture diagram, restyles equations and tables, and adds shock maps, sensitivity plots, super-resolution/timing tables, and confidence-interval figures. Existing spectral and correlation figures are largely retained and reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens component attribution, empirical breadth, uncertainty reporting, and transparency about computational costs—important gaps in v1's support for accuracy and efficiency claims. Sections 5 and Appendices K–N provide the decisive gains. Some limitations remain: the noise analysis excludes an unstable run, and the claim of best results on all TRL3D metrics conflicts with LSM's lower one-step vRMSE in Table 5. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvement in evidence and practical qualification.
